J_integrator.interpretation: Every z=0 contour result is diagnostic only. Integrator UNKNOWN is preserved verbatim, including any z-invariance reason. This experiment does not prove full-domain 2D behavior or physical G.

assumptions: straight z-axis crack front
z-invariant antiplane Mode III field, u_x=u_y=0
linear isotropic elasticity with supplied positive shear modulus
closed contour around the front with outward normals
integrator_result.normal_convention: outward from the enclosed front region; positive signed area required
integrator_result.field_provenance: direct readback from frozen solved coefficients; source result SHA256=39cb2dabe767998baf5e84b038f39510d6ef7db10bcd6c77298b480045cb24d3; volume level=volume_gl4x8x4; provider rows bound by canonical semantic coefficient IDs

budgets.tracked_array_estimate_scope: adapter-held arrays and provider values/gradients; provider MLS/exact-field internals and Python object overhead are excluded

limitations: The coefficient values are read from the existing frozen solve result; the adapter does not assemble K or invoke the static solver.
The exact field reference is used only inside the frozen basis provider and as an independent scalar J comparison; solved field outputs come from phi/dphi contracted with the solved coefficients.
The full gradient, including its native z component, is passed unchanged to the frozen J integrator.
A z=0 contour is a midsection diagnostic and cannot establish full-domain two-dimensional behavior, path-independent physical G, or crack-growth readiness.
